summary: Dragana Majhen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA (1999) under Michael Hahn and a PhD (2004) at the University of Marburg, holding posts there (attested 2002, 2020) and at the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Dror Burstein is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2014 and teaches literature at Tel Aviv University.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Reed College (~1987–1991) and Harvard University (~1993–2000), later holding posts at UC Irvine (~1999–2006) and UC Berkeley (~2006–2011).
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lozang Trinlé was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Gyuto Monastery and under Ngawang Yönten. He was a professor at Minzu University (~1959–1965), Director of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences, and taught at Tibet University (~1985–1997).
Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under teachers R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, as well as under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.

Durgamohan Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Scottish Church College, Vidyasagar College, and the University of Calcutta, where he also held an academic post.

Dwijendra Nath Shukla was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor K. A. Subramania Iyer and held a post at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

Dylan Esler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Buddhist Studies from SOAS University of London and completed his PhD (2018) at KU Leuven, where he also worked as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology who studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo, and Khenpo Rinchen. In 1990, he was a professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies scholar and Tibetologist. He studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded and directed Nitartha Institute (~1996) and held posts at Nalanda West and Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College (~1978–1983) and SOAS (~1984–1986), as well as under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin.

Dörte Kamarid works in Tibetology and Indology. She studied at the University of Vienna, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, with Helmut Tauscher supervising her MA.

Tibetologist E. Gene Smith studied at institutions including the University of Washington and Leiden, under teachers such as Turrell V. Wylie and Dezhung Rinpoche. He held posts at the Library of Congress and founded and directed the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
E. H. Johnston was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held a professorship at the University of Oxford (attested 1940).

E. Michael Mendelson was a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge (~1946–1949), the University of Paris (~1949–1953), and the University of Chicago (~1953–1956).
E. W. Adikaram was a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of London, where he studied under William Stede (attested 1946).

Eberhard Sandschneider is a scholar of Sinology and other fields who studied at Saarland University (~1974–1981). He held positions at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (1995–1998), Free University of Berlin (1998), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).
